title: Pre-Analysis — Retrofit Extension of the Slat Piccolo Duct Support Bracket Redesign
abstract: Closed pre-analysis of the retrofit extension of the slat piccolo duct bracket redesign to the pre-cut-in fleet, prompted by continued duct low pressure reports from three operators.

sections.objective: Establish whether the redesigned piccolo duct support brackets, in production since the 2022 cut-in, can be offered as a retrofit to the aircraft below it, and what that costs in leading edge access and in documentation. Three operators had continued to report wing anti-ice duct low pressure on one wing, and fleet support wanted a position before the next winter season rather than after it.
sections.findings_summary: Five items were confirmed and none blocking, which is why the retrofit was recommended. The fault isolation procedure for duct low pressure is the most valuable of them: it currently sends the technician to the duct joint seals first and to the bracket last, which on the evidence of the three operators is the wrong order for pre-cut-in aircraft. Correcting it would recover most of the reported downtime even on aircraft that never take the retrofit. The production bulletin covers completion to the new standard but is written for line completion, not for in-service embodiment, and needs a retrofit variant. The position and leak check quotes bracket positions from the old geometry. The leading edge harness runs through the same bays. Separately, a candidate relocating the bleed overheat sensing elements needs the same access and should be embodied in the same visit.
sections.next_steps: Reorder the fault isolation procedure and release it ahead of the retrofit, since it helps the whole fleet. Commission a retrofit variant of the completion bulletin. Correct the bracket positions in the leak check and add the post-retrofit table. Update the clamp position references on the leading edge wiring sheet in the same package. Coordinate the leading edge access window with the bleed sensing relocation candidate before either is planned, and give fleet planning a combined estimate so the winter season target is assessed against one opening rather than two.

similarity_seeds: duct low pressure on one wing traced to a support bracket rather than a seal
fixed leading edge access shared between anti-ice and bleed work

tasks.title: Search anti-ice and leading edge content on ATA 30-10 and 57-20
Review the fault isolation ordering against the operator reports
Assess leading edge harness routing through the affected bays
Identify candidate changes needing the same access

expected_findings.rationale: The procedure checks the duct joint seals before the support bracket. On pre-cut-in aircraft the bracket is the more probable cause by a wide margin, so the current ordering costs the operator a full leading edge opening before it reaches the real fault.
expected_findings.resolution: Reorder the procedure and release it ahead of the retrofit, since it benefits aircraft that never take the bracket change.

expected_findings.rationale: The existing bulletin covers completion to the new bracket standard on the line, where the leading edge is already open. As an in-service instruction it omits the access, the drain provisions and the reinstatement checks entirely.
expected_findings.resolution: Commission a retrofit variant of the bulletin with full access and reinstatement content.

expected_findings.rationale: The position and leak check quotes bracket positions measured from the original support geometry. On a retrofitted wing those measurements do not correspond to anything.
expected_findings.resolution: Add a post-modification position table to the check.

expected_findings.rationale: The leading edge harness for the anti-ice valve and slat position sensing runs through the same bays the brackets sit in. Retrofit work disturbs the clamping and the harness sheet shows the clamp positions against the old bracket flanges.
expected_findings.resolution: Update the clamp position references on the wiring sheet in the same package.

evidence.similarity_note: Retrieved on similarity alone. Both are described as work inside the fixed leading edge requiring the bay to be opened, one in anti-ice duct support language and one in bleed overheat sensing element language. No shared part number, functional item, zone or ATA chapter.

expected_findings.rationale: The sensing element relocation candidate needs the same bays opened. If both are planned separately the leading edge is opened twice on the same aircraft, and the relocated sensing elements are routed past the brackets this retrofit changes.
expected_findings.resolution: Coordinate a single leading edge access window and route the sensing elements against the post-retrofit bracket flanges.

expected_non_findings.reason: Comes back on the shared ATA 57 wing chapter and on repair language about panel access, but it is a scarfed composite patch on the lower cover with no duct, bracket or bay content and no shared part number or zone.

type_data.conclusion: Closed. The retrofit was recommended and the fault isolation reordering was released ahead of it as a fleet-wide benefit independent of embodiment.
